machine#5.name: Resume mismatch guard: stop when record and branch disagree
machine#5.problem: After many power-offs a session's task record and its branch can drift apart. A released session may start fresh over commits its record does not cover, duplicating or discarding work.

machine#6.name: Resume from the run journal; retry at the tail
machine#6.problem: An account session limit can kill a run midway. Re-running everything wastes tokens, and a cached failure could be wrongly served as a result.
machine#6.mechanism: Stable unique agent labels and a deterministic call order; completed agents replay from the journal, dead ones replay null instantly; retries go at the tail with a per-attempt label; resume passes resumeFromRunId and knownDead. No Date.now; stamps come via args.

machine#7.name: Circuit breaker on session limit
machine#7.problem: When the account session limit is hit, issuing more agents only produces nulls and hides what did not run.
machine#7.mechanism: Readers run in slices of five; two or more fresh nulls in one slice halts issuing, accounts for every unstarted id as not_started, logs HALT and returns.

machine#8.name: Checkpoint and resume by dependency hash
machine#8.problem: After a stop, an agent cannot tell which files it relied on have changed, so it either trusts a stale handoff or re-reads everything. Work is lost or redone.
machine#8.mechanism: A stdlib Python tool (tools/coding_workflow.py) hashes task.md, a context packet and chosen source files into a JSON checkpoint; resume re-hashes and lists changed or deleted dependencies. Unrelated changes do not invalidate it. A verify command and pre-commit hook sit beside it.

machine#21.name: Dead locks after a boot; commit and push at every green checkpoint
machine#21.problem: The PC lost power for 28 minutes at about 13:25 on 13 November and cut off eight lanes mid-turn. Stale slots and tickets could have blocked every lane afterwards.
machine#21.mechanism: A lock or ticket older than the last boot is treated as dead, because process ids are reused. Lanes commit and push at every green checkpoint; the coordinator restarts Docker Desktop and wakes each lane with a resume message.

machine#24.name: Leave the antivirus alone; unpack from official archives

retrieval#1.name: Co-change floor (files that changed together)
retrieval#1.problem: Provide a cheap baseline for 'what else changes with this file' taken only from git history, which any graph must beat.
retrieval#1.mechanism: From ancestor commits only, count how often files changed in the same commit, rank by support and confidence with a recency weight, and return the top files within the token budget. Same-PR sibling commits are dropped.

retrieval#1.results: Held-out T1 recall 0.638 +- 0.033 (M); TUNE 0.752 (M). Top-ten precision 0.26, with PageRank 0.28 (M). Typed beats it by +0.063 [0.019, 0.110] but only on mobile seeds; on backend seeds co-change 0.709 vs typed 0.699 (M).

retrieval#35.name: Abstaining retrieval: miss, candidate or lead
retrieval#35.problem: At a few hundred entries a wrong hit acted on is the dangerous failure and a miss is cheap; raw search scores cannot serve as confidence, and a repair-time lookup must never leak customer data into the store.
retrieval#35.mechanism: Canonicalise and scrub (phones, CNIC, placeholders), exact-handle prefilter, three-table BM25 ranking, then abstain on score-free features (exact hit, IDF-weighted coverage, margin). Output is miss, candidate or lead, max one of each, inside a 2,000-character cap; a write gate refuses duplicates and self-matches.
